questions.question: How do custom properties differ from Sass variables?
questions.answer: Custom properties are live CSS values that participate in the cascade and inheritance, can be read/overridden at runtime, and work in DevTools. Sass variables are compile-time substitutions that disappear from the output.

questions.question: How do var() fallbacks work?
questions.answer: var(--name, fallback) uses the fallback when the custom property is missing or invalid. The fallback can itself be another var() or any valid value.

questions.question: How does inheritance make theming possible?
questions.answer: Custom properties inherit, so a variable declared on :root reaches every element. Overriding it on a subtree (e.g. [data-theme=dark]) re-themes only that subtree without touching component rules.

questions.question: How do you support OS dark mode and an explicit toggle?
questions.answer: Set default tokens on :root, override them in @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), and add an explicit [data-theme=dark]/[data-theme=light] override for user choice. Also set color-scheme for native controls.

questions.question: What does @property add to a custom property?
questions.answer: It registers a type via syntax, sets inheritance, and gives an initial value. Typed properties can be validated and smoothly animated/interpolated (e.g. angles, colors).

questions.question: Create semantic light/dark tokens and apply them to a card.
Why does a custom property with an invalid value break the declaration?
questions.answer: Custom properties are substituted before validation; if the resulting value is invalid for the property, the declaration becomes invalid at computed-value time and falls back to inherited/initial behavior. A var() fallback only helps if the property is missing, not if it is present but invalid.

questions.question: Why can't an unregistered custom property animate smoothly?
questions.answer: Without @property it is an untyped string, so the browser does not know how to interpolate it. Registering a syntax (e.g. <angle>) enables typed interpolation and animation.
